messages:
Ava (PM): Heads-up — we have three enterprise customers asking for stronger isolation + regional routing guarantees. Want to align on roadmap tradeoffs this quarter.
Priya (Arch): Thanks. Are they asking for hard region pins or softer affinity + SLA tiers?
Marcos (Sales): Two customers want data to stay in EU region (hard), one wants latency guarantees across APAC with fallback. All are asking about phased migrations.
Rafi (Eng): Implementation-wise we can do affinity + soft pinning quickly, but hard pins need capacity reservations and placement constraints. Cost and bin-packing hit is nontrivial.
Liam (SRE): Also operational complexity — hard pins increase cold start risk and complicate failovers. Need runbook changes + eviction policy.
Ava (PM): For roadmap: propose Q3 deliverable = "Affinity + SLA tiers" (soft pins + contractual SLOs). Q4 = "Hard residency lanes" (region pins + reservation). Thoughts?
Priya (Arch): I support staged approach. We should define clear launch criteria for each phase. For Q3: metrics: 99th p99 latency delta < 20ms vs baseline for affinity, cost delta < 15%. For Q4: need capacity commitment model and automated admission control.
Rafi (Eng): Agreed. For Q3 work, we can extend current routing policy DSL with two flags: prefer_region and sla_tier. Example policy proto: ```policy { match: tenant_id prefer_region: "eu-west-1" sla_tier: "gold" }```
Marcos (Sales): Customers will push for fleet guarantees. We need a pricing/commitment doc in parallel so we don't sell unsupported promises. I can draft language.
Liam (SRE): Operational acceptance criteria: canary traffic for 48h with no more than 3 incidents, automated fallback to global pool, and playbook for regional evacuation.
Priya (Arch): Also include telemetry and alerting: routing decisions, cache hit rates, percent of requests served from preferred region, and per-tenant fallback counts.
Ava (PM): Good. Who owns the migration plan for Q4 hard pins? We need an ops-friendly path: staged tenant onboarding, quota checks, dry-run mode.
Rafi (Eng): Eng owns migration tooling; will build a dry-run that simulates placement constraints and flags tenants that would be capacity-excluded. ETA: prototyping in 3 sprints.
Priya (Arch): Spec note: we must ensure model variants compatibility across regions (quantized vs full precision). Routing should prefer compatible variants or trigger model-fallback.
Marcos (Sales): Customer asks about contract language for fallbacks — they want guaranteed behavior if region fails. We need to map that to SLOs we can support.
Liam (SRE): Fallback behavior: documented sequence: same-region replica -> paired-region -> global pool. Each step should have an expected RTO and known performance delta.
Ava (PM): Let's capture launch acceptance criteria for the Q3 affinity feature: 1) API stable and opt-in flag; 2) Dashboard metrics surface per-tenant affinity; 3) Canary rollout path and rollback hooks; 4) Cost impact analysis and a mitigation plan.
Priya (Arch): Add: security/compliance checklist for region residency (KMS, audit logs) must be satisfied before GA for any tenant claiming residency.
Rafi (Eng): Dev note: will add feature flag per-tenant and route evaluation cost budget. We should also add automatic prefix/KV cache affinity to reduce cross-region cold misses.
Marcos (Sales): I'll coordinate customer pilots for the Q3 feature — two reference customers available in EU and APAC. Timeline looks ok if eng hits prototype.
Ava (PM): Decision: scope Q3 = affinity + SLA tiers + telemetry + pilot customers. Q4 scope sketch = hard residency lanes + capacity reservations + migration tooling + updated legal SLOs.
Liam (SRE): Ops asks: schedule a runbook dry-run 1 month before Q3 pilot and a chaos exercise post-canary.
Priya (Arch): Long-term: consider a policy catalog with templates (low-cost global, latency-first, residency-first) and a policy compiler that projects capacity/cost.
Ava (PM): Action items: Rafi — prototype DSL flags + dry-run tool (3 sprints). Priya — spec telemetry and policy templates (2 weeks). Liam — ops runbook draft (2 weeks). Marcos — pricing/contract language and pilot signups (1 week). I'll consolidate into a roadmap PR.
ops-bot: Reminder: Please add proposed PR link to #release-war-room before EOD Fri. :bell:
Marcos (Sales): acked, will put contract draft in the PR.
Rafi (Eng): will post a short spike doc with design tradeoffs today.
Priya (Arch): I'll sketch the policy templates and a sample capacity projection model.
Ava (PM): Thanks team — next sync in one week to review spike results and firm dates.
